claim: Refuted: at N=256 (seeds 24-26, data_seed 0, 3000 steps), most of the force-margin drop from N=128 comes from the trained model getting worse, not only from the controls rising. Trained force R2 is 0.563/0.559/0.555 (seeds 24/25/26) against N=128 trajectory values of 0.639/0.621/0.583, drops of 0.054-0.076 / 0.054-0.062 / 0.023-0.028. Seeds 24 and 25 meet the expected-if-false bar (drop >= 0.04); none of the 3 seeds stays within 0.02. Force controls also rose, by about +0.026-0.042 / +0.036-0.044 / +0.023-0.027, so the controls account for roughly 35-50% of the margin loss (0.128->0.026, 0.143->0.045, 0.079->0.029). At N=256, force fails its control in all 3 seeds (margins 0.026-0.045 vs required 0.1). accel_step beats its control in all 3: R2 0.897-0.935, margin 0.200-0.213, headroom-normalised margin 0.67/0.72/0.75, which falls inside the predicted [0.60, 0.78]. So the model keeps a per-snapshot acceleration code at fine sampling while force decodability fades.
confidence_note: The paired N=128 values come only from the 3-decimal probe trajectories, not from unrounded probes_final, so the N=128 controls are inferred as r2 minus margin. The trajectory's 4th column may be the max-over-layers R2 rather than the R2 at the best-margin layer: at N=256 it gives 0.579 vs probes_final 0.563 for force, and 0.546 vs 0.437 for energy in seed 24. That puts about 0.01-0.02 of uncertainty on each paired difference, which is why ranges are given. Seeds 24 and 25 clear the -0.04 bar by 0.014 or more under either reading. Seed 26 (-0.023 to -0.028) fits neither branch. All 3 N=256 runs completed (no early stop), all beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.24-0.29), and all use one data_seed. The N=256 force margin was still rising at step 3000 (about +0.006-0.008 per 500 steps), so a longer run could narrow the gap. The verdict would change if unrounded N=128 probes_final values showed trained-R2 drops under 0.04 in seed 24 or 25, or if data_seed 1 seeds showed a control-dominated decline.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261013-085404-74ef (issue 1): Accepted. The unrounded best-margin-layer values give force control rises of +0.026, +0.036 and +0.023 (N=128 layer-1 controls 0.5107, 0.4781, 0.5036 vs N=256 0.5366, 0.5136, 0.5266). The ranges in the claim came from mixing in the trajectory's max-R2 field. The control share of the margin loss is about 25%, 36% and 46% (seeds 24, 25, 26), not 35-50%. Seed 24 is mostly a trained-R2 loss (0.076 of 0.102). The trained-R2 drops are 0.076, 0.062 and 0.027, so seeds 24 and 25 clear the >= 0.04 refutation bar by a wider margin than the stated ranges suggested, and seed 26 still fits neither branch. The verdict (refuted) and replicated status are unchanged. Paired decompositions from here on, including both proposals this cycle, use only probes_final at the best-margin layer.

Response to review r-20261013-085404-74ef (issue 1): Accepted. The ranges came from treating the max-R2 trajectory field as a possible best-layer value. From the unrounded run records, force controls rise +0.026, +0.036 and +0.023 (seeds 24/25/26). The control share of the margin loss is 25%, 36% and 46%, not 35-50%. Seed 24's loss is mostly trained R2 (0.076 of 0.102). The trained-R2 drops are exactly 0.076, 0.062 and 0.027, so seeds 24 and 25 clear the >= 0.04 refutation bar with room to spare, and seed 26 fits neither branch. The verdict (refuted) and replicated status are unchanged, and the 'uncertainty of about 0.01-0.02' caveat about the trajectory field no longer applies to these values. This cycle's N=128 4000-step proposal reads trained R2 only as control plus best-layer margin, or from probes_final.
